3.2 Annual Plans: 14-Day Money-Back Guarantee
 CloudScale provides a 14-day money-back guarantee for annual enterprise plans, subject to two strict requirements:
 • Submission Window: The refund request must be delivered in writing within 14 calendar days of the initial
    service activation date.
 • Usage Limit Requirement: Total compute usage during the initial 14-day window must remain under 50
    computing hours. If telemetry logs show 50 or more computing hours consumed, the annual subscription becomes
    strictly non-refundable.
 • Post-14-Day Cancellations: Requests submitted after the 14-day window are non-refundable. Platform access
    continues until the end of the paid 12-month term.

3.3 Monthly Subscriptions Refund Policy
 Monthly subscriptions are strictly non-refundable once the monthly cycle begins. Cancellation terminates future
 renewal charges, and services remain active until the end of the current 30-day period without partial or prorated
 refunds.

3.2 Definition of Downtime and Calculation Formula
Downtime is defined as any continuous period of one (1) minute or more where covered platform services
are completely inaccessible across all availability zones, or where the HTTP server error rate (HTTP 5xx
responses) exceeds five percent (5.0%) across all valid customer API requests. The Monthly Uptime
Percentage is calculated using the following standard formula:
                                                                                             
                                       Total Scheduled Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes
     Monthly Uptime Percentage =                                                                × 100
                                                   Total Scheduled Minutes in Month
Service availability is measured by automated synthetic probes executing health checks every sixty (60)
seconds from five external global regions (US-East, US-West, EU-Central, AP-East, and AU-Southeast).

Monthly Uptime %         Enterprise Credit       Professional Credit
                                                                        Application Mechanism
99.90% to < 99.99%        10% of Monthly Fee     SLA Target Met (0%)    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
99.00% to < 99.90%        25% of Monthly Fee      10% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
98.00% to < 99.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      25% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
95.00% to < 98.00%        50% of Monthly Fee      50% of Monthly Fee    Applied to subsequent billing invoice
< 95.00%                 100% of Monthly Fee     100% of Monthly Fee    Maximum allowable monthly credit
                      Table 2: Service Credit Compensation Brackets by Subscription Tier

4.4 Credit Rules and Maximum Limitations
• Monthly Cap: Total service credits issued in any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the
   customer’s monthly recurring fee for that month.
• Non-Refundable: Service credits cannot be exchanged for cash refunds, wire transfers, or credit card
  chargebacks.
• Sole Financial Remedy: Service credits constitute the customer’s sole and exclusive financial remedy
  for downtime.

  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING SUM(downtime_minutes) > 0

JOIN subscriptions AS s ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN monthly_incidents AS m ON m.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.tier = 'Enterprise'
  AND c.status = 'active'
  AND s.payment_status = 'paid'
ORDER BY c.customer_id;

database_results.sql:
WITH monthly_downtime AS (
    SELECT
        c.customer_id,
        c.company_name,
        s.billing_cycle,
        s.monthly_rate,
        SUM(i.downtime_minutes) AS total_downtime
    FROM
        customers c
            JOIN
            subscriptions s ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
                JOIN
                incident_tickets i ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id
    WHERE
        c.tier = 'Enterprise'
        AND c.status = 'active'
        AND s.payment_status = 'paid'
        AND s.billing_cycle = 'monthly'
        AND i.reported_at >= '2024-02-01'
        AND i.reported_at < '2024-03-01'
        AND i.status = 'resolved'
    GROUP BY
        c.customer_id,
        c.company_name,
        s.billing_cycle,
        s.monthly_rate
),
credit_calc AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        company_name,
        billing_cycle,
        monthly_rate,
        total_downtime,
        (1.0 - (total_downtime * 1.0 / 41760.0)) AS uptime,
        CASE WHEN total_downtime > 0 THEN 15 ELSE 0 END AS applicable_credit_percentage,
        CASE WHEN total_downtime > 0 THEN (monthly_rate * (total_downtime * 1.0 / 41760.0) * 15 / 100) ELSE 0 END AS credit_amount
    FROM
        monthly_downtime
)
SELECT
    customer_id,
    company_name,
    billing_cycle,
    monthly_rate,
    ROUND(uptime, 6) AS uptime,
    applicable_credit_percentage,
    ROUND(credit_amount, 2) AS credit_amount
FROM
    credit_calc
WHERE
    total_downtime > 0
ORDER BY
    customer_id;

SELECT c.customer_id, c.company_name, s.billing_cycle, s.monthly_rate, SUM(i.downtime_minutes) AS total_downtime FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id JOIN incident_tickets i ON c.customer_id = i.customer_id WHERE c.tier = 'Enterprise' AND c.status = 'active' AND s.payment_status = 'paid' AND i.reported_at >= '2024-02-01' AND i.reported_at < '2024-03-01' AND i.status = 'resolved' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.company_name, s.billing_cycle, s.monthly_rate HAVING SUM(i.downtime_minutes) > 0;

### 1.2 Subscription Cycles and Billing Options

CloudScale offers two recurring subscription billing options for enterprise accounts:

- Monthly Billing Cycle: Subscriptions are invoiced every 30 calendar days in advance. This option provides operational agility with no long-term contractual commitment.
- Annual Billing Cycle: Subscriptions are prepaid in advance for a continuous 12-month period. Clients selecting the annual billing cycle receive an immediate 15% upfront discount relative to standard monthly rates across all compute tiers and base platform licenses.

CloudScale measures service availability monthly across each calendar month. The uptime target represents the percentage of scheduled minutes during which covered services remain reachable, responsive, and error-free.

### 2.3 Enterprise Net-30 Payment Terms

Enterprise tier customers may apply for Net-30 payment terms, granting 30 calendar days from the invoice issuance date to settle balances. Approval requires satisfying three mandatory prerequisites:

- (a) Commercial Credit Check: Passing a formal corporate credit risk assessment approved by CloudScale Finance.
- (b) Financial Documentation: Submitting two consecutive years of audited financial statements or three verified commercial credit trade references.
- (c) Minimum Contract Threshold: An active contract with a Minimum Annual Contract Value (ACV) of at least $24,000 USD (or 24,000 EUR).

### 5.3 Ongoing Incident Communication Cadence

During an ongoing active incident, CloudScale provides regular progress updates until the issue is resolved:

- Severity 1 Incidents: Enterprise customers receive status updates every 30 minutes; Professional customers receive updates every 2 hours.
- Severity 2 Incidents: Enterprise customers receive status updates every 2 hours; Professional customers receive updates every 6 hours.

On March 15, 2024, each asks for a cash refund of unused subscription time instead. Explain the refund treatment for the monthly and annual members using their recorded activation dates.
input_context: Treat the database as a fixed supplied snapshot. Its account/payment statuses are snapshot labels, not a historical status ledger. Do not infer a past account state from those labels. Use the stated policy versions for the exercise; do not invent later revisions.

For cases calculating monthly credits, assume all recorded downtime in the specified month is qualifying, non-overlapping downtime, that the incident list is complete for that month, and that subscriptions remained covered throughout that month. Assume other credit prerequisites and timely filing are satisfied unless the question explicitly asks about them or provides different facts. These are exercise assumptions, not facts recorded in the database.

For credit amounts, treat monthly_rate as the applicable final monthly recurring fee, already reflecting any contractual discount. Do not apply the 15% annual discount again. The database has no currency column: report amounts as currency units, unless the question supplies a currency. Ignore taxes for credit calculations.

Use actual calendar-month lengths in UTC: January and March 2024 have 44,640 minutes; February 2024 has 41,760 minutes. Do not use the SLA's illustrative 30-day allowance for every month. Compare unrounded uptime against bracket thresholds; round displayed uptime to six decimal places and money to two decimal places.

For annual refund-window questions, use subscriptions.start_date as initial activation for the exercise. Do not substitute customer join dates or renewal dates. The database does not prove new activation at renewal or record refund requests, compute usage, claim filings, or invoice due dates.

Cite both PDFs by document and page/section, and expose the SQL and its raw result. Use an actual calculator tool for arithmetic when exercising the full system. Equivalent read-only SQL and equivalent supporting passages are acceptable.

For this question only, all three monthly_rate values share the same unspecified currency unit, allowing a meaningful sum. Without this assumption, the DB has insufficient currency information to justify a monetary total across customers.

required_answer_facts.fact: The cohort consists exactly of Nexus, Vanguard, and Solaria.
Nexus credit amount is 1050.00 currency units.
Vanguard credit amount is 240.00 currency units.
Solaria credit amount is 450.00 currency units.
The supplied shared-currency assumption is required for this total.
Nexus has no partial refund for an already-started monthly cycle.
Solaria has no partial refund for an already-started monthly cycle.
Vanguard is beyond 14 days from initial activation on March 15, 2024.
Renewal does not establish a restart of the initial-activation guarantee.
No SLA credit may be converted to cash.

prohibited_claims: Sum amounts without the visible common-unit assumption.
Convert any service credit to cash.
